rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Civil Code Section 1947.12)
rules.requirement: An owner may not raise the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months. A sitting tenant's rent may be raised in no more than two increments in a 12-month period, and the owner may set the initial rent freely for a new tenancy.
rules.key_value: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park), for rent increases after the initial rent of a tenancy is set.

rules.exemptions: Deed- or agreement-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or K-12 school; housing under local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than this cap; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, provided tenants received the required written exemption notice; an owner-occupied two-unit property where neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU, while the owner continues in occupancy; homeowners of a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive relief, damages equal to rent collected above the maximum, discretionary reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times the excess for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief; actions must be brought within three years.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.interaction_text: (3) Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity’s valid exercise of its police power consistent with Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50) that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).
